_notes: Single source of truth for every setting shared between the lab notebooks and
scripts/gate_hybrid.py in the authoring repo. The gate's job is to predict what
the room will see, so any value that differs between the two makes the gate a
Notebooks fetch this file, and it points at the golden CSVs, by commit rather than
by main, so an edit here reaches nobody's notebook until the pinned commit in
templates/ is moved to it on purpose:
Add a setting here before adding it to a notebook, not after.

_max_tokens: null means the parameter is omitted from the request entirely and the model
generates up to its own limit. Do NOT delete the key to get this: llama-index's
OpenRouter class defaults max_tokens to DEFAULT_NUM_OUTPUTS = 256, which is the
setting that made every answer 'Empty Response' and invalidated the first gate run.
Omitting the argument and passing None are opposites here.
context_window stays set explicitly: it defaults to 3900, which silently splits
five retrieved chunks across multiple refine passes.
_sample_sizes: lab_sample_size is the number of questions a notebook shows row by row: Lab 2-B's
per-question table, Lab 3's fusion trace, its prompt task and its expansion table. No score
is computed on it any more: retrieval is scored on every quality-1.0 question, which costs
one batched embedding call rather than a judge call per question.
gate_sample_size and judge_model are read by scripts/gate_hybrid.py in the authoring
repo, not by any notebook, since the labs stopped scoring answers with a judge (2026-10-21).
lab_sample_size was 10 until the 2026-09-21 pre-flight audit, and 15 since.
_model_string_forms: The same model needs a different string depending on which library calls it, and
getting this wrong fails in two different unhelpful ways. Keep both spellings.
llama_index.llms.openai.OpenAI validates names against its own
table and raises on 'openai/gpt-4.1-mini' even with a correct
api_base, which is why Lab 3 uses the OpenRouter class.
litellm_chat_model   'openrouter/' prefix. For LiteLLM, which routes on the prefix.
embed_model          'openrouter/' prefix. For LiteLLMEmbedding, same reason.
Lab 2 deliberately uses nano rather than mini: it is a prompting and chunking lab and
runs many more calls per attendee, so the cheaper model is the right default there.
_langchain: LangChain's ChatOpenAI talks to OpenRouter by pointing base_url at it and passing the
key. Model strings then take OpenRouter's own unprefixed form, the same spelling the
llama-index OpenRouter class wants, NOT the 'openrouter/' prefixed LiteLLM form.
comparison_models is the small/large pair Lab 0 puts side by side.
_retrieval_metrics: How Labs 2 and 3 score retrieval, with no judge and no generation. Both labs run one
shared cell, word for word (tools/check_notebooks.py fails if the copies differ). A
retrieved chunk 'holds' a golden passage when it contains at least hit_threshold of the
passage's shingle_size-word runs, after lowercasing and stripping markup and punctuation.
The golden passages came from different chunks than either index (PyMuPDF-era text, against
pypdf text in Lab 2 and LlamaParse markdown in Lab 3), so an exact-match rule would miss most
true hits. Per question, over the top k chunks:
hit@k         some chunk holds the passage
source hit@k  some chunk from the question's own source file holds it
recall@k      the share of the passage's shingles found anywhere in the k chunks
MRR@k         1/rank of the first chunk that holds it (0 if none does)
k is similarity_top_k for every table; depths are the extra k values the depth tables show.
Every question with synthetic_input_quality == quality_filter is scored, not a sample.
Differences between two retrievers carry a 95% interval from ci_resamples resamples of the
questions (seed random_state). These follow the documented definitions of the authoring
side's retrieval_metrics.py (6-word shingles, a 50% share of the golden passage).
_rrf_k: The k in reciprocal rank fusion. Not passed anywhere: llama-index 0.14.24's
QueryFusionRetriever hard-codes k = 60 and counts ranks from 0, so a chunk at 1-based
rank r adds 1/(60 + r - 1). Lab 3's fusion trace starts from this value and lets
attendees try a smaller one, so the trace and the retriever agree by default.

behr.label: Behr technical data sheets
_corpus_variants: Same documents, same chunk budget, same embedding model. Only the splitter differs, so
the gate can answer whether header-aligned boundaries retrieve better than sentence ones
instead of that being assumed. Build the second with:
python scripts/build_improved_nodes.py --splitter markdown \
--out-name improved_nodes_markdown.parquet
Only sentence is published as a release asset; the variants are local measurements.
s1024ov0 is the control, sentence at overlap 0. It exists because the markdown path in
split_document packs header sections and never applies chunk_overlap, so markdown against
sentence compares two things at once. Measured 2026-09-22: markdown is not distinguishable
from sentence on this corpus either way (recall@5 -1.5%, 95% CI -6.5% to +3.3%), and the
hit@5 drop of 6.7 points is two questions that arrived in two chunks rather than one.
See review-docs/FINDINGS-markdown-splitter.md.

calhr.label: CalHR employee benefits
_chunking: 384/96, not Behr's 1024/200, and this is the one place the datasets differ on
purpose. CalHR is a sixth the size: at 1024/200 it splits into about 100 chunks and a
top-5 query retrieves roughly 5% of the whole corpus, so dense retrieval finds the right
chunk by accident and hybrid has nothing to win.
CORRECTED 2026-09-21: the pre-build estimate said 384/96 would give 290 chunks and a
1.7% top-5 share. The real build gives 255 chunks and 2.0%. The estimate was made by
splitting pymupdf text before the LlamaParse run existed, and it predicted the real
figure would come in higher; it came in lower. The choice still stands, but it is nearer
the edge of the within-2x-of-Behr target than the original note claimed.
Phase 4c in TODO-list.md has the full table and the gate results.
_corpus_variants: c384 is 384/96, the original decision. c256 is the recorded fallback, built after the
gate failed at c384: naive 2.940 beat hybrid 2.913 with 19 of 30 questions tied all ways.
Only the chunk budget differs; same parse, splitter and embedding model.
md384 and s384ov0 were added 2026-09-22 to answer the markdown splitter question. md384 is
the header-aware build at the same budget; s384ov0 is sentence at overlap 0, the control,
because the markdown path never applies chunk_overlap and would otherwise be credited or
blamed for it. Result: md384 loses 14.5 points of recall@5 against c384 (95% CI -22.5% to
-5.8%, 24 of 30 questions worse), but 9.7 of those points are the missing overlap alone.
What is left for the header boundaries is not distinguishable from zero.
See review-docs/FINDINGS-markdown-splitter.md.

_dataset_assets: table_exhibit and chunk_pages are paths in this repo, fetched at the same pinned commit
as this file (a notebook derives the base URL from its own config URL), so set_pin.py
moves them with everything else. table_exhibit: one complex table shown three ways for
